Currently, for vSphere Cloud Provider, if node vm is deleted, the node is left `notReady`. This Change will delete that `notReady` node
```

**Related code**
`InstanceExistsByProviderID` here will return `false, error` if no instance is found.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.16.7/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/vsphere.go#L728-L742
But it should check if it's VM is deleted not shutdown, then return `false,nil`

And it should cherry pick this fix avoiding deleting shutdown node https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70291

**What you expected to happen**:
After VM is deleted, the node should be deleted, pods assigned to the node should be rescheduled to other available nodes
**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Deploy k8s cluster. In our case we use PKS.
2. Deploy workloads on node
3. Delete worker node VM from IAAS
```
govc vm.destroy -vm.ipath /vm-ed40fae0-56d3-4c7a-a0dd-b9ac53684294
```

```
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:

We do not have any other power state other than 3 mentioned here. What is the objective of checking against them?

I think the main objective of this function `Exists` is to make sure VM is present on the inventory, regardless of the it's power state.

Hi @divyenpatel , there are only 3 states for VM https://github.com/vmware/govmomi/blob/3decde69e9aa0bcc8a831e3f87acae26c2151c4a/vim25/types/enum.go#L4573-L4575
Also I cherry picked this changes from this commit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70291/files
Hemant explained here why he added this check https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70291/files#r229045231
It's to protect against any other state in the future sdk
Do you anticipate not found fault here? if yes then we need to interpret it as VM not exist and return true.
